Here at @hiddenpearlbk we take great pride in our vast Japanese Whisky selection, and a favorite has to be @takaminewhiskey 

Aged 8 years and crafted with history. 🥃
@takaminewhiskey is a tribute to Dr. Jokichi Takamine’s pioneering spirit—using koji fermentation. Koji converts starches into sugars, a technique traditionally used in sake and soy sauce production, setting it apart from conventional malting processes. 

With hints of cherry, green apple, dark chocolate, and a finish that lingers with oak, tea, and toasted grain, this one is oh so easy to sip on.

📸: @hahonie

The Shinigami ☠️✨

Also known as The God of Death, this yōkai is a dark spirit believed to guide people towards the afterlife.

Bright passionfruit and zesty yuzu leads with vibrant acidity. Honey adds depth, while yellow bell pepper introduces a subtle, savory sweetness. Tequila blanco and @cardenxesotol swirl like the winds of the afterlife-providing a smooth, earthy warmth. Finally balanced out by a ghostly touch of ponzu and hemp milk clarification , as if brewed by the hands of the Shinigami itself.

The Shinigami is mysterious, powerful and a haunting reminder of mortality — and whatever  unseen forces may bring it to be. 🪦

Created by head bartender @victoriadegirasoles

So excited to finally share this project with everyone! This is a collection of Yokai inspired shot glasses created for the best bar in Brooklyn, @hiddenpearlbk !!

What are Yokai you may be wondering? 

Yokai are Japan’s legendary spirits—sometimes spooky, sometimes silly. Think demon cats with glowing eyes, two-headed figures lurking in the dark, and mischief in every shadow. I love their weird, wild energy and felt such inspiration and excitement creating this collection.
Thank you so much to @hiddenpearlbk for the opportunity.

Please come take a shot with me and try all the amazing new drinks for spring!

Summers in Italy 

- Gin, Vermouth di Torino Rosso, Cucumber Cordial, Meyer Lemon, Fresh Basil, Sea Breeze 

As the dew sings
Crushed basil in bloom
As the Garden whispers 

How to build:
- 1 oz Bordiga Rosso Di Torino Vermouth 
- 1 oz Bordiga Occitan Italian Gin 
- .75 oz Cucumber Cordial 
- .75 oz Meyer Lemon Juice 
- 6-8 Basil Leaves 
- 1 dash of Saline

Garnish:
- Fresh Basil Leaf 

-Muddle the basil gently in a shaker—just a light press to release aromatics, don’t tear it up.
- Add saline, cucumber cordial, meyer lemon juice, gin, vermouth.
- Add 4 KD cubes hard shake.
- Double strain into a coupe or Nick & Nora glass to keep it clean.
- Garnish with a basil leaf on rim.

Fire Waltz is what happens when s’mores get dressed up for a night out. ⁠
⁠
Gourmet all-natural marshmallows are gently roasted over classic graham crackers. A duo of organic sauces (caramel & Mexican chocolate with a hint of heat) are drizzled over the top and the whole thing is tied together with our addictive bourbon maple chocolate pecans.⁠
⁠
It's the perfect way to end (or start) your time at Kissa Kissa -- an upgraded familiar favorite.⁠
⁠
As for the name, "Fire Waltz" is one of jazz pianist Mal Waldron's most enduring compositions. First recorded in 1961 with Eric Dolphy and Booker Ervin on Waldron's Prestige Records LP "The Quest," this song features two contrasting horn lines that weave together seamlessly just like the sauces on the plate.⁠

caption:
When the weather turns cold, there's nothing quite like the warming comfort of a hot toddy. It's Nina's favorite on a chilly night, so we invented one with a uniquely Kissa Kissa spin: Dusk Fire 🔥 ⁠
⁠
It's a sultry little hot toddy with smoke, spice, and just enough burn to keep you warm ’til last call.⁠ Instead of traditional black tea, we utilize Chinese lapsang souchong. It's distinctively smoky brew is achieved using a pinewood fire to dry out the tea leaves.⁠
⁠
Deadwood bourbon is the other main attraction in this mug, balanced out by saffron liqueur, honey, a kiss of lemon, and a gently torched rosemary sprig for a final aromatic touch.⁠
⁠
The name "Dusk Fire" comes from the title of a 1966 LP by England's Don Rendell/Ian Carr Quintet. It was the second of a series of five flawless records the fivesome laid down at Lansdowne Studios between 1965-'69. ⁠
⁠
It's one of those under-appreciated gems we love spotlighting on the turntables here at Kissa Kissa and is a worthy namesake for this revamped classic cocktail!⁠

caption:
Passion Dance: tequila, passionfruit, a hint of heat. It's a cocktail that sways somewhere between sweet and sultry just like its namesake.⁠
⁠
McCoy Tyner first recorded "Passion Dance" on his 1967 Blue Note outing The Real McCoy and it instantly worked its way into the canon of modern jazz standards. ⁠
⁠
The original version finds Tyner's intricate chordal comping backing a sprightly melodic statement shared with tenor saxophonist Joe Henderson. It's a spiraling, indelible tune that carries echoes of the pianist's long association with his dear friend John Coltrane while remaining distinctly Tyner's own.⁠
⁠

Cue the ghosts of Impulse! past.⁠ Tonight’s set: candlelight, minor chords, and a cocktail that knows your secrets -- Stolen Moments 🎃⁠
⁠
Named after the opening track of Oliver Nelson's 1961 masterwork The Blues and the Abstract Truth, "Stolen Moments" is an intoxicating, swirling composition which has been tackled by legends like Carmen McRae & Betty Carter, Herbie Mann & Chick Corea, Eddie Davis, Ahmad Jamal and Kenny Burrell.⁠
⁠
Stolen Moments the zero-proof cocktail is hypnotically ripe, floral, and delicious. Passionfruit, lime, and orange juices are rounded out by herbal flourishes and whispers of elderflower. It's the perfect drink for anyone looking for an alcohol-free option during a ghoulishly good night out⁠

caption:
Something we get asked about frequently is the sound system here at the kissa. It was custom-designed for the layout of our physical space by the wizards at @tmr_audio in Erie, Colorado and optimized for an elevated jazz listening experience.⁠
⁠
It all starts with our turntables, a pair of SL-1200GR2s sponsored by Technics and Nagaoka MP-500 cartridges. ⁠
⁠
Those pass through a rotary mixer to our electronics, which were built specifically for Kissa Kissa by the talented ModWright team in Amboy, Washington. The hardware there includes an LS 99 tube preamp and twin KWA 99 monoblocks.⁠
⁠
Finally, a rich spectrum of sound makes its way out through our speakers, the stars of which are our Harbeth Audio pairs: a couple of Super HL5+ XDs and a Compact 7ES-3 duo that fill the space beautifully no matter where you find yourself seated.⁠
⁠
Of course, you don't need to be an audiophile (or even a jazz lover) to enjoy your time here with us. But if you are, our hope is that we can treat you to  one of the nicest sounding spaces in Brooklyn!⁠
⁠

caption: Playing around with cocktail photography is seriously one of our favorite things. At our all time favorite Kissa Kissa in Brooklyn.

💌 Handle with care: our new Airmail Special has landed!⁠
⁠
🛬 A daring new cocktail for our adventurous friends, this drink turns the foundation of the century-old Airmail drink recipe upside down with a whirlwind of Vietnamese flavors.⁠
⁠
🇻🇳 The star of the show is our vibrant housemade bánh mì shrub. It's a punchy and potent infusion of rice vinegar, sugar, and the classic flavors of your favorite street food sandwich.⁠
⁠
🌱 To further heighten the profile, we've introduced additional harmonies into the mix. Think lemongrass, kaffir lime, Thai basil, jalapeño, ginger, cilantro...⁠
⁠
🍸️ Then we marry and mellow the shrub's bold acidity with both blended white rum and a pleasingly herbaceous, high-proof rhum agricole, lime juice, and the fizzy sweet kiss of our natural house pét-nat wine.⁠
⁠
😋 We hope you'll find the end result to be a truly unique and well-balanced drink that will transport your taste buds someplace new!⁠
⁠
➕️ Gnawing that lemongrass stalk garnish a before your sip = drinksmaxxing⁠
⁠

#ARevivalSZN - On July 23 I have my third session as a guest record selector at @kissakissa.us - a jazz vinyl bar in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. For this set I’m celebrating saxophone legends like Sonny Rollins, John Coltrane, Dexter Gordon + more. 

I plan to continue these sessions each month, with a theme that celebrates jazz artistry, music history or Black culture. Comment “PEACE” if you want the link to my newsletter for updates. I’d love to see you in the building. When you come through, here are a few things you can expect!

1 - Dress Code🪞: There will be wavy people in the building. All type of waves. Comfortable and fly asl in a vibey fit. It is Brooklyn, after all. 

2 - Drinks and Bites 🥃 : The drinks are fantastic. Cocktails (and a few mocktails) are all named after jazz standards and there are multiple options for each spirit. I’m partial to the whiskey section, particularly the drink named after Thelonious Monk’s classic, ‘Round Midnight. Light snacks are also available.

3 - Intentional Listening 🤌🏾: I select my records from the venue’s enormous collection of vintage jazz vinyl. They have over 5,000 titles listed in their database, and they are all in great condition. Since 2024 I’ve been building my own personal vinyl collection, which features a range of genres from gospel to funk, soul to rap. But in deference  to the venue’s vision, I play solely jazz music from their collection. 

I play records like a music artist because I am one. That means you won’t hear mixes or transitions like you would with a traditional DJ, because artists usually want listeners to experience our music in full. And because I curate the music with deep intention for a sonic and narrative arc, I don’t really do requests. I hope you can trust the ride!

While you’re listening you should absolutely carry conversations, meet new people, and enjoy your time. Remember, too, that many folks will be there *just* to indulge in the sounds pulsing through the venue’s dynamic sound system. 

I look forward to vibing with you. 🙏🏾

-3/10 🍷 What a week, what a year, what a life. I am truly sorry to my 4 fans for the delay in content. I tend not to post when life is going well, so take that as a barometer for what’s to come. For the other 123 followers, why are you here? And here’s a reminder to unfollow me, it’s all downhill from here, and you probably don’t actually like me. This rating is for the wine, but also for what came after it. Ironically, my last post was regarding a certain 27 year old who I spent one hell of a season with. Unsurprisingly, they don’t age like fine wine, and this one didn’t mature as fast as the 173 bottles of Barolo we drank together. From a 32 year old man-child with a married twin flame and an existential crisis, to a 27 year old who loved himself more than he could ever love me, it’s no surprise I drink entirely too much wine. In the midst of straddling generations, I spent a dreary Saturday at the dreamiest baby shower. True to Jeanie beanies roots, New Orleans reigned. Cocktails, food and company were five stars. Feathers, family, friends, and frolicking were the heart of the party. But, let me be clear, this was the absolute worst red wine I have ever let enter my body. Was it blueberry maple syrup that a drunk New Yorker made with salt instead of sugar? Was it non alcoholic in respect to my surrounding sober friends? Whatever it was, it belonged in hell. I’ve never not finished a red until now. But don’t dwell, I spent the next 9.5 hours getting absolutely blasted enough to ruin my fake relationship. A few lessons to my 2 followers who have gotten this far (do I thank you or recommend you to my therapist), 1) don’t ever drink for 10 hours straight and believe you are sending a coherent text (idiot), 2) don’t ever try and finish a wine that smells like your cat just peed on your face, and 3) don’t ever let yourself be with a man who isn’t mature enough to handle you after a few terrible glasses of red wine. Onto the next glass.

Moe’s Doughs in Greenpoint doesn’t just make an apple fritter, they make THE apple fritter.

Let’s address the headline first. For five dollars, you get a pastry roughly the size of your face and close to a pound in weight. That alone borders on absurd. But scale without execution means nothing, and this is where Moe’s separates itself.

The exterior fries to a deep, craggy crunch, creating pockets of caramelization that shatter on contact. Inside, the crumb stays tender and properly enriched, never greasy, never doughy. Chunks of apple are folded generously throughout, softened, spiced, and still tasting like fruit rather than filler. The glaze clings just enough to add sweetness without muting texture.

What makes this fritter exceptional is balance at scale. Big pastries usually collapse under their own ambition. This one holds. Every bite delivers contrast: crisp and soft, sweet and lightly spiced, indulgent but somehow composed.

A little holiday update post— with creative credit going to friend and team member @purr_bnb, who knows how to laugh with me and at me. Because without a sense of humor, I’d never make it as a rescuer.

The past 7+ weeks have been full of pain, tears, and struggle, as I came to terms with an injury that wasn’t going to fix itself—and ultimately landed me in emergency surgery last week. “Not me. Not now,” I kept saying. Alas, it was me, and it was now.

This didn’t mean rescue work came to a halt. It did mean slowing down and leaning on others—including an incredible team of volunteers who stepped in, in every way imaginable. I never felt so powerless, and at the same time, never felt more grateful for the team, the community, the outpouring of support. 

While I’m not yet 100% back on my feet, I’m 100% still committed to the work that needs to get done—and to the cats in our care (including some newly rescued ones… more on that tomorrow!). And for that, we continue to rely on your support: from drivers to fosters to friends and donors. 

Tonight, we have two cats hospitalized—one who underwent surgery today, and another who suffered a spinal injury and was rescued on the very same day (my birthday!) that I learned I would need spinal surgery myself.

How grateful am I to be in a position to be able to help others as I continue to heal myself. It would never be possible, without all of you. 

Thank you ❤️

Special thanks to @purr_bnb @meowis.house @putitonmytabbies @greenpoint_haus_of_pussies @catsinthecityny  @leonardstkitties @tinytigersnyc @brooklynkittycommittee @aramg83 @hollyesque @greenpointvetcare and sister Meg who never looks at her Instagram no matter how many times I ask her to please look at her Instagram. I probably forgot some people and for that and many other things I will continue to use “anesthesia side effect” as an excuse. You know who you are. Xoxo - Becky

As the holiday season approaches, maintaining physical well-being becomes especially important amid colder weather, busy schedules, and increased physical demands. At Complete Physical Therapy, our focus is on helping patients stay active, resilient, and pain-free during this high-activity time of year. Whether you are managing a chronic condition, recovering from an injury, or addressing new aches brought on by seasonal stress or winter conditions, our individualized physical therapy programs are designed to support safe movement and long-term function.

The holidays often involve travel, prolonged standing, lifting, and changes in daily routines—all of which can aggravate musculoskeletal issues. Our licensed physical therapists emphasize evidence-based care, hands-on treatment, and targeted therapeutic exercises to improve mobility, strength, and balance. At Complete Physical Therapy, we work collaboratively with each patient to reduce pain, prevent injury, and promote sustainable recovery, allowing you to fully participate in holiday activities with confidence and comfort. As the year comes to a close, prioritizing physical health is one of the most valuable investments you can make for a stronger, healthier start to the new year.

EKSYUS ME! 🇵🇭 KA BA? | EPISODE 4 | Meet Abi Balingit, Baker, Cookbook Author

Today I got to hangout with Abi Balingit (@theduskykitchen), the bright and colorful baking sensation behind "Mayumu: Filipino American Desserts Remixed"

Born out of the pandemic, her debut book, "Mayumu" recounts Abi’s recipes that blend traditional Filipino flavors with Western baking while speaking on her experiences as a Filipino-American. "Mayumu" was named one of The New York Times’ Best Cookbooks of 2023 and won her the 2024 James Beard Award for Emerging Voice — one of the highest culinary honors in the US and an award that only 7 Filipinos hold.

When asked what she thinks makes a good baker? Her answer is simple. Sharing. 

From sharing your recipes to sharing your success with your community, Abi believes that the foundation of a good baker is the ability to put yourself out there and understand that you are the only one that can limit your own talent by not allowing the world to see your work. 

Speaking of sharing work, apart from her book, you can find a few of Abi’s creations out there like her @clementinesicecream Pandan Polvoron Raspberry Cheesecake Ice Cream on @goldbelly and her Filipino Pepperment Baked Alaska made with chocolate Bibingka at @kelloggsdinerbk

Thank you for a wonderful morning, Abi! If I didn’t get to say it myself — I am so so effin proud of you and your work for our community. 💚

Ouroboros, 2025
Oil on linen, 20 x 16”

The Ouroboros is an ancient symbol depicting a snake eating its own tail, associated with wholeness, regeneration, and the cycle of eternal return. I’ve spent a lot of time thinking this year about how painting has a tendency to feed upon itself, so I decided to paint myself a little snack about it with some works that have inspired me embedded inside. 

They say that objects in the rear view mirror are closer than they appear, but be careful - prolonged reflection into the past has a way of obscuring the present. 

PS: watch out for the rotten cherry.

As we wrap 2025, there is so much to be grateful for at birdhouse. 

First and foremost, to our Safekeepers: thank you for creating environments that activate curiosity, honor the child, and keep our classrooms alive. ✨ Learning here often feels like a game of improv - the practice of “yes-anding” children’s ideas and following them into the depths of their curiosity. We see them. And we recommit to seeing them every single day.

To our families: the culture of birdhouse was never predetermined. It has been built day over day with the children and the families who bring their rituals, values, and engagement into our School Family. We are lucky to call you our partners in this work.

And to our birdies 🐣 whose curiosity is boundless, who show up bravely each day with big ideas and big feelings, courageous enough to let us in.

This year was shaped by many moments:

🛶child-led investigations like our Boat Study, where we explored floating, sinking, building, revising, and collaborating

 🎶morning songs that set the tone and ensure every child is seen

🚕 outdoor time exploring the sounds and elements of Brooklyn

🧘yoga and mindfulness, building body awareness and emotional regulation

⛑️ a visit from our local fire station, sparked by the children’s curiosity

🐱gentle, patient care with Khaleesi, our school cat 🐾

🤝 Family Education Night, where we slow down and build community together

And above all, the quieter moments you could miss if you don’t pay attention - the big emotions, the gut belly laughs, two new friends holding hands, the tenderness of an older child helping a younger child zip their jacket, the intrinsic joy when a child builds upon a new skill. These are the ones we live for. 

As we head into 2026, we’re deeply grateful for this community and excited for what’s ahead ✨

@artmeccanyc Artist: @craig_anthony_miller 
Gallery Partner: @theclistcocktailbar 
Exhibit: “Equinox Celebration”
Date: 9/19/2025
Time: 6pm-9pm
Location: 835 Franklin Ave, Brooklyn, 11225
Artist Bio: Craig Anthony Miller (b. 1971) was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York. He received his BFA in graphic design from @stjohnsu in Queens, New York. His professional graphic art practice gave way to his natural transition into painting. The opportunity to share his creative process at a live painting event on the Lower East Side in 1996 was the first in a series of events that would lead him to shift his focus primarily to painting. 

Working primarily in acrylic and aerosol paints, both in studio and public spaces, CAM has created a series of paintings and murals that combine the style of stained glass and the energy of the urban landscape with symbols of freedom, strength, resilience and well-being.

He targets Meditation and Mindset with a personal quote of “Always Be Mindful Of Your Ability to Fly” and “Keep your Head To Your Crown.” Productions of work feature the Hindu Deity Lord Ganesh, as well as birds- a popular symbol for freedom of flight. The “Pursuit of Nectar” Series -represented by the hummingbird- holds many positive symbolic interpretations, making it another very effective totem.

To learn more about our artists, clients & services, please visit ArtMecca.com & #lhartclub. With Art Mecca, you are the gallery.

Is Dyker Heights worth adding to your NYC bucket list? 

I finally went and here’s what you should know.
Would I recommend it if you’re short on time or visiting NYC for the first time? Honestly… maybe not.
 But if you love Christmas lights, local traditions, and something different from Midtown chaos, Dyker Heights is a fun detour.

Good to know before you go: • Dress warm, as everything is outdoors • please be mindful that it’s a residential area • During the weekends they have hot chocolate and snacks for sale • Guided tours are available, or take the R train to Bay Ridge

Crowds can get intense, so weeknights are the best time to visit if you’re looking for a more relaxed experience.

With love, care, and pure intention, we continue to create positive impact within our communities — and our Purple Christmas Celebration is a true reflection of that mission.

Purple Christmas started because our founder once experienced the holidays while living in a domestic violence shelter and understood firsthand how heavy that season can feel for survivors and their children. What began as a way to bring warmth, dignity, and joy into shelter spaces has grown into a tradition rooted in community, healing, and hope. This event is deeply personal to us, and it represents everything Sisters In Purple stands for: showing up, loving loudly, and making sure families know they are not alone.

This was more than a toy drive — this is what it looks like when a community comes together with the right intentions. From laughter and smiles to moments of genuine connection, our children left feeling like they were surrounded by family that truly loves and cares about them. ☕🎨🎄

We extend our deepest gratitude to the partners who helped make this moment possible:
💜 @riseprojectnyc 
💜 @projectechony 
💜 BK Alumnae Deltas
💜 Xi Phi Omegas
💜 The Harlem Sigmas
💜 New York Achievement Foundation 
💜 New York Alumni Chapter of Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity
💜 Delta Mu Zeta Chapter
🎥: @thecareerplug 

A heartfelt thank you to @shestillgotthejuice from Jumpin Jen’s, our amazing decorator and hostess with the mostest — from hot cocoa and cookie decorating to coloring, games, and joyful activities, she created a space where our children could simply be kids and feel deeply cared for.

And a huge shoutout to @angies.dad , who stepped in like a true superhero to provide our community with fresh haircuts, helping our families feel confident, seen, and uplifted during the holidays. 💇🏽‍♂️🦸🏾‍♂️

Thank you to every donor, volunteer, and supporter who made our families feel loved and reminded them that hope is real and people truly do care.

We are so excited to watch Purple Christmas continue to grow bigger and brighter each year — because when we move with intention, community becomes magic. 💜✨

Technique of the week: easily sliding over to mount from side control.

If we try to get to mount from side control using just head and arm control, my partner can endlessly spin with me since his shoulder is free to move, allowing him to use space to start recovering his guard.

What we want to do is open up our chest and scoop our arm underneath their elbow, which gives us double unders control. Now we can easily slide into joint with little resistance from our partner.

E pensar que, meses atrás, quando nos mudamos para o mesmo bairro (não mais ao lado da Equinox), eu decidi começar a treinar no prédio e revezar com a academia.

Eu não fazia barra livre sem trava — tinha medo de me lesionar. E o personal @marcelo_augusto_cf , que me acompanha há anos, falou: “𝒸ℴ𝓂ℯ𝒸𝒶 𝓈ℯ𝓂 𝓅ℯ𝓈ℴ, 𝓈ℴ𝓂ℯ𝓃𝓉ℯ 𝒸ℴ𝓂 𝒶 𝒷𝒶𝓇𝓇𝒶.”

E foi exatamente isso que eu fiz.

Hoje, colocar o peso de 35 de cada lado e conseguir executar 10 repetições com tranquilidade me trouxe uma felicidade enorme!!
O que a constância e a disciplina diária podem fazer… Elas nos levam a desenvolver uma força que nem imaginávamos ser capazes de ter.
Estou usando o exemplo dos meus treinos físicos diários (sem pausas), mas isso vale para qualquer área das nossas vidas.

Adventures with KJC about Aurora in Brooklyn:

⸻

If you’re looking for rustic charm and authentic Italian flavors in Williamsburg, Aurora is the spot. Since 2003, this gem has been serving up handmade pastas, vibrant antipasti, and house-made desserts that transport you straight to Italy without leaving Brooklyn.

The vibe? Warm exposed brick, high ceilings, and a lush garden patio that’s perfect for brunch, date night, or a celebratory dinner with friends. 

Favorites to try: their Prosciutto e Burrata, squid-ink pastas, and the tonnarelli cacio e pepe (a must for cheese lovers). And don’t forget to save room for gelato. 

Whether you’re going for the food, the atmosphere, or the photos, Aurora has a little something for everyone. Definitely a stop worth making on your next Brooklyn adventure.

📍 Aurora — 70 Grand Street, Williamsburg, Brooklyn

“Vegetables” 

They are the quiet keepers of the earth,
born without voices, yet fluent
in the grammar of light.

Each root is a small labyrinth,
each leaf a map of forgotten winds.
They remember rains we never saw,
and the first fire that ever touched a kitchen.

To cut one open
is to open a secret archive:
the green script, the hidden geometry,
the slow, patient dream of the world
becoming nourishment.

In their silence
they teach the oldest lesson—
that the universe grows itself
into shapes we can hold in our hands
and taste.

28 days in quiet darkness. Seconds in Nancy’s fire.
Highland Hollow ribeye crossing the threshold—
and the music says the rest.
Break on through.

Chef Nicholas Leiss @chef__nicholas_leiss leads Maison Sun’s kitchen with the calm precision of a craftsman and the curiosity of a naturalist. His cuisine is rooted in the micro-terroirs of the Hudson Valley and shaped by reverence for the Lenape and Canarsie peoples, whose ancestral lands give life to Brooklyn and its surrounding waters.

A former protégé of Günther Seeger and Tom Colicchio, Leiss learned the discipline of restraint — flavor drawn from patience, clarity, and exacting technique. His cooking reflects the purity he absorbed at Fäviken, the quiet inventiveness he honed at Noma, and his own distinct sensibility: rigorous, humble, and elemental.

At Maison Sun, he explores how local landscapes can speak in global dialects. Butter is churned from Hudson Valley cream, grains are fermented into miso, and smoke is drawn through cedar and pine — a dialogue between the soil of New York and the spirit of the Silk Road.

Fire meets tide.
The sea remembers its shape.

MAISON SUN Dining Experience in Brooklyn

Last night, I had an amazing dining experience at @maisonsun.nyc, where gastronomy meets art. Maison Sun is a Modern Asian restaurant located in Boerum Hill, Downtown Brooklyn. With a focus on artistry and fine dining, Executive Chef Zhaojin Dai (former Executive Sous Chef at Michelin rated Jungsik and Restaurant Yuu) is behind every exquisite dish that blends French techniques with Asian traditions. I tried a 7-course tasting menu, artfully presented at an all-stainless steel counter beside an open kitchen with a vintage Molteni stove. Everything was so delicious and artfully presented. My favorites were the Lobster Tartare and Charcoaled Striped Sea Bass. The desserts were so good too! It’s definitely a must-try experience. 

Tag and share with someone who would love this restaurant. 

📍Location: 200-3 Schermerhorn St, Brooklyn, New York City

Some places are impossible to call just restaurants. They are more than just dinner—they are a journey, unfolding with every dish, every nuance of flavor, every moment. 🌟

@maisonsun.nyc is exactly that kind of place. With only 14 seats, each one is positioned for the perfect view of the magic happening in the kitchen. 👀🔥 Chef Zhao Jing Dai creates true culinary masterpieces, blending the elegance of French techniques with the finesse of Asian traditions. 🍽️🇫🇷🇯🇵

The winter menu is a seven-course experience, where every ingredient is revealed in a new light. ✨ The lobster tartare with yuzu and pine nuts is pure freshness, lightness, and sophistication in one bite. 🦞🍋 And the A5 Kagoshima Wagyu striploin? A deep, unforgettable flavor that melts in your mouth. 🥩🤤

Everything here is designed to surprise: the perfect balance of flavors, the meticulous attention to detail, and an intimate atmosphere that feels almost sacred. 🍷💫 The service is impeccable—subtle yet intuitive, anticipating your desires before you even voice them. 🛎️✨

Maison Sun is a place you’ll want to return to. For the flavors, for the emotions, for the artistry woven into every dish. 🎭❤️

Chef Raffaele Solinas is an award-winning Italian chef and vice President of the Italian Chefs Association of New York (AICNY). Born and raised in Sardinia, his culinary philosophy is rooted in tradition, technique, and the preservation of regional Italian excellence. With an international career spanning five-star hotels, global cruise lines, and New York City’s competitive dining scene, Chef Solinas is the force behind three acclaimed restaurants: Osteria Brooklyn LIC, Osteria Brooklyn DeKalb, and Osteria Brooklyn.

In addition to leading his restaurants, he offers bespoke private chef services and curated culinary events, and has represented Italian culinary heritage through United Nations–aligned cultural initiatives. Deeply committed to education and mentorship, Chef Solinas also supports Italian language and cultural foundations dedicated to promoting authentic Italian cuisine as the gold standard in New York City.

The Right Bank of Bordeaux, also known as the Libournais area, is a wine region in France located east of the Dordogne River and the Gironde estuary. Right Bank wines are known for their bold, complex character, with flavors of dark fruit, licorice, chocolate, and spice. They are typically made with a blend of 70% Merlot, 15% Cabernet Franc, and 15% Cabernet Sauvignon, but may also include Petit Verdot and Malbec. The Merlot gives Right Bank wines a smoother texture and softer tannins than other Bordeaux wines, and they are often described as “drink me soon” style wines that can age but are best enjoyed relatively young. The Right Bank’s clay, limestone, and gravel soil is also considered ideal for growing Merlot and Cabernet Franc. 
 

Left Bank vs. Right Bank in Bordeaux: What’s the Difference?

The wine regions that are located to the east (right) of the Dordogne River are considered part of the Right Bank. The regions that are located between the two rivers and to the west (left) of the Garonne River are called the Left Bank.

✨Dinner Dreams at MUSE THAI Brooklyn! ✨

📍MUSE THAI @musethai 
📍689 Washington Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238

Started in spring 2017, MUSE quickly became the heart of Crown Heights’ restaurant scene. This gem serves up comfort food where fresh, finger-licking Thai dishes arrive hot from the kitchen to tables filled with friendly faces, stories and laughter. Each season, the team crafts menus preserving authentic Thai flavors while adding creative twists for Thai-style tapas that the neighborhood absolutely loves! 💕🍽️

FAIR WARNING though!!! 🚨 These portions are MASSIVE for the price - seriously don’t over-order like we did! 🙈

Started with the ROCK SHRIMP and I’m still dreaming about them! 🍤 These jumbo crispy babies tossed in that chef’s special sauce had me fighting my friends for the last one! The BBQ PORK is marinated Thai-style perfection - so tender and flavorful you’ll want to order seconds! 🔥

The PEANUT DUMPLINGS were such a unique bite! Sweet turnip wrapped in fresh rice with red onion and ground peanut - the texture combo is everything! 😍

THE WHOLE CRISPY BRANZINO though!!! 🐟 Not just a dish - it’s a FEAST for only $39.95! This perfectly crispy whole fish comes with the most incredible green chili avocado sauce made with special curry paste, Thai herbs, coconut milk, pineapple and avocado. Value. Pack. Goals. 🙌

The Small Island “Khao Soy” is NEXT LEVEL! 🍜 This Northern Thai curry with coconut cream, egg noodles, veggies and the BIGGEST chicken wings you’ve ever seen could literally feed two people! So warming and perfect for these chilly nights! ❤️

But the showstopper? That Beef Rib Massaman Curry! 🥩 The rib is literally ARM-SIZED and braised until it’s melt-in-your-mouth tender, swimming in savory massaman curry with coconut milk, potato and avocado. Comes with roti bread and rice to soak up every bit of that sauce! 🤤

Finished with the perfect Mango Sticky Rice - the ideal sweet ending to this epic feast! 🥭

As we wrap 2025, there is so much to be grateful for at birdhouse. 

First and foremost, to our Safekeepers: thank you for creating environments that activate curiosity, honor the child, and keep our classrooms alive. ✨ Learning here often feels like a game of improv - the practice of “yes-anding” children’s ideas and following them into the depths of their curiosity. We see them. And we recommit to seeing them every single day.

To our families: the culture of birdhouse was never predetermined. It has been built day over day with the children and the families who bring their rituals, values, and engagement into our School Family. We are lucky to call you our partners in this work.

And to our birdies 🐣 whose curiosity is boundless, who show up bravely each day with big ideas and big feelings, courageous enough to let us in.

This year was shaped by many moments:

🛶child-led investigations like our Boat Study, where we explored floating, sinking, building, revising, and collaborating

 🎶morning songs that set the tone and ensure every child is seen

🚕 outdoor time exploring the sounds and elements of Brooklyn

🧘yoga and mindfulness, building body awareness and emotional regulation

⛑️ a visit from our local fire station, sparked by the children’s curiosity

🐱gentle, patient care with Khaleesi, our school cat 🐾

🤝 Family Education Night, where we slow down and build community together

And above all, the quieter moments you could miss if you don’t pay attention - the big emotions, the gut belly laughs, two new friends holding hands, the tenderness of an older child helping a younger child zip their jacket, the intrinsic joy when a child builds upon a new skill. These are the ones we live for. 

As we head into 2026, we’re deeply grateful for this community and excited for what’s ahead ✨

📍French Louie (@frenchlouienyc ) 

Weekend brunch in Brooklyn that hit all the marks. Here’s what we had:

1️⃣ Crab Benedict on Croissant: Instead of the usual English muffin, this came on a buttery croissant layered with sweet crab meat. The poached eggs were rich and silky, finished with hollandaise and scallions for brightness. Luxurious without being too heavy. 
2️⃣ Shoestring Fries: Crisp, salty, and dangerously snackable. Served with both aioli and ketchup (I went heavy on the aioli). Perfect for sharing…though I definitely didn’t want to.
3️⃣ Aperol Spritz: Light, refreshing, and just the right pairing with this brunch spread.

✨ The Experience:
The cozy dining room and neighborhood vibe made this a perfect weekend spot. French Louie nails that balance of elevated but approachable - exactly the kind of brunch that leaves you full, happy, and already planning a return trip.
